producer_report.summary: Root cause: usage was kept in four places (each job's `invocations` list, plus the steward, audience and auditor lists), and nothing guarded the list of sources or the list of roles. A measure author could read one source without knowing of the others and so retire active roles. The base commit already held the source fix: `Records::all_invocations`, the split documented on `JobRecords::invocations`, the system fact, and a `role need` measure that reads only `all_invocations`. This change closes the gaps that let the class reopen. (1) A test-only `ALL_ROLES` list in `store.rs`, with a test that scans the `Role` enum source and fails if a variant is missing, duplicated or unparsable. (2) The `from_parts` store test now loops over `ALL_ROLES`, so a role or list added later must come back out of `all_invocations`. (3) `MEASURED_ROLES` is hoisted to a const in `role_need.rs`, and a test requires every role to be measured or on demand, never both and never neither. (4) A new output test, `every_role_loaded_through_from_parts_is_counted_and_classified`, loads one run of every role in each of 10 closed jobs through the real `Records::from_parts` and asserts on `RoleNeed::compute`'s output. Every role has a count above 0. Steward, audience and auditor have source `SOURCE_OUTSIDE_JOBS`, are unflagged, are in `not_measured`, and are not retire candidates. (5) A CHANGELOG bullet names the root cause. No refusal rule was added, so no refused-share number applies. Docs, spec, status, display, lib and shard-timings already matched the code on grep, so I left them unchanged.

open_issues: The role-driven `from_parts` test cannot catch a fourth list that is not keyed by a new Role, for example routing an existing role by a condition. `from_parts` routes by role only today. The doc comments on `JobRecords::invocations` and `Records::all_invocations`, and the source-scan test in role_need.rs, are the only guards for that case.
No replay over real records was possible: the snapshot has no measure data to replay beyond the test fixtures, and records/ is absent from the working copy.
mistakes: My first full `cargo test --locked` was started in the background with the default timeout and was stopped at the limit, so I had to run it a second time.
learnings: The base commit already held the source fix for this class (`Records::all_invocations`, the split documented on `JobRecords::invocations`, the system fact, the spec text, the known-active replay tests and the CLI test), so the work was guards, not the fix itself.

`Role` is defined in athena-data/src/records.rs. A new variant already breaks the build at `Role::as_str`, but a hand-written list of roles in tests can be silently incomplete; the enum-source scan is what catches that.

role_need.rs has a source-scan test that forbids `.invocations`, `steward_runs`, `audience_runs` and `auditor_runs` in non-`//` code before `#[cfg(test)]`. New doc comments there must avoid those words (`//!` and `///` lines are skipped).
Producer shell policy blocks tail, grep and echo in Bash and blocks reading outside the working directory, including the background-task output file; completion arrives as a notification.
A background `cargo test` holds the build slot, so a foreground cargo command exits 75 until it finishes. Background commands stop at the default 600000 ms unless `timeout` is raised.
